title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection is usually document-level or task-specific token-level, leaving a gap in unified fine-grained localization. TokenCore builds a memory bank of normal BERT word-level embeddings using max pooling and scores test tokens by nearest-neighbor distance, with mean aggregation for document scores. On three token-annotated datasets, TokenCore ranks first in average AUROC at both token and document levels, including token-level Grammar AUROC 0.6371.

match_target.why: The user hint explicitly asks for TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset. No Table 3 appears in the provided paper, so the closest available value is Table 1's TokenCore Grammar token AUROC 0.6371. This is cheap to reproduce on the 300-document Grammar set and still supports the paper's claim that TokenCore ranks first on Grammar at the token level.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score printed in [0, 1], the Grammar dataset has 300 documents, and the paper reports no std or CI for this value. Use 0.02 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: Use the three token-level text anomaly datasets introduced in the paper: SMS Spam, Restaurant Review, and Grammar Correction.
requirements.quote: we construct three benchmark datasets spanning different types of textual anomalies: corrupted characters, semantic anomalies in reviews, and grammatical errors.

requirements.stmt: Use both document-level and token-level annotations for evaluation.
requirements.quote: Each dataset is carefully curated to include both document-level and token-level annotations, enabling fine-grained anomaly localization.

requirements.stmt: For Grammar Correction, use the stated evaluation construction: 270 correct sentences as normal and 30 incorrect sentences as anomalous.
requirements.quote: We construct our evaluation set by selecting 270 correct sentences as normal samples and 30 incorrect sentences as anomalous samples

requirements.stmt: Use BERT-base-uncased embeddings as the shared representation for TokenCore and baselines.
requirements.quote: All the methods operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation.

requirements.stmt: Aggregate BERT subword embeddings to word-level token embeddings using element-wise max pooling.
requirements.quote: To maximize the anomaly signal for each token, we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings.

requirements.stmt: Build the TokenCore memory bank from word-level embeddings of all normal training samples.
requirements.quote: During training, we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: Score each test token by the distance to its nearest neighbor in the normal memory bank.
requirements.quote: At test time, for each token with embedding etest, we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank

requirements.stmt: Use a distance metric consistent with the paper's example, Euclidean distance, for nearest-neighbor scoring.
requirements.quote: where d(·, ·) denotes the distance metric (e.g., Euclidean distance).

requirements.stmt: Obtain document-level anomaly scores by mean aggregation of token-level scores over all tokens in the document.
requirements.quote: To obtain document-level anomaly scores, we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document.

requirements.stmt: Use 50% of normal documents for training and the remaining data, including both normal and anomalous documents, for testing.
requirements.quote: We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with AUROC and AUPRC; for the target claim, compute token-level AUROC.
requirements.quote: We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Compare TokenCore against the seven-method table setting: LOF, iForest, ECOD, Deep SVDD, AutoEncoder, LUNAR, and TokenCore.
requirements.quote: Table 1: Evaluation results across 7 anomaly detection methods in terms of AUROC and AUPRC.

requirements.stmt: Interpret larger nearest-neighbor distance as a higher token-level anomaly score.
requirements.quote: A larger distance indicates higher anomaly score, as the token is farther from any normal token pattern in the embedding space.

requirements.stmt: Implement TokenCore as a text-domain adaptation of the PatchCore memory-bank paradigm.
requirements.quote: TokenCore adapts the memory bank paradigm from PatchCore [10] in computer vision to the text domain.
